title: HTML Foundations
subtitle: Build real web pages with HTML and see every change live
intendedFor: Absolute beginners and students preparing for CSS, JavaScript, frontend development, or full-stack development.

courseOverview.recommendedSequence: Complete modules in order. Every technical topic connects HTML source to the live browser preview.
courseOverview.summary: A practical beginner HTML course covering documents, text, links, images, lists, tables, semantic structure, forms, metadata, accessibility, and a complete single-page capstone.

moduleSummary.title: First Web Pages
moduleSummary.coreSkill: Understand HTML as document structure that a browser parses and renders.
moduleSummary.outputFocus: Combine document structure, headings, paragraphs, and basic attributes in one page.

moduleSummary.title: Links, Images, and Paths
moduleSummary.coreSkill: Create links with anchor elements and useful link text.
moduleSummary.outputFocus: Build a profile page with text, links, and an accessible image.

moduleSummary.title: Lists, Tables, and Structured Content
moduleSummary.coreSkill: Choose ordered or unordered lists based on content meaning.
moduleSummary.outputFocus: Combine lists and a data table into a clear information page.

moduleSummary.title: Semantic and Accessible Page Structure
moduleSummary.coreSkill: Use header, nav, main, and footer to describe major page regions.
moduleSummary.outputFocus: Build a page with landmarks, navigation, article content, and accessible structure.

moduleSummary.title: Forms and User Input
moduleSummary.coreSkill: Connect labels to form controls and understand form structure.
moduleSummary.outputFocus: Build a complete form with labels, sensible input types, choices, and a submit button.

moduleSummary.title: Final Capstone: Personal Website
moduleSummary.coreSkill: Bring document structure, semantic HTML, forms, metadata, and accessibility checks together.
moduleSummary.outputFocus: Build and verify one complete semantic, accessible personal website.

authoringGuidance: This course uses profileId web, workspaceProfileId browser-web-runner, and workspacePolicyId html-browser-workspace.
Hands-on HTML tasks use kind code_input, fixedLanguage web, recipeType source_checks, and index.html.
Every code_input must include explicit sourceChecks and must not include stdout tests.
Use source_regex when harmless whitespace or attribute ordering should be accepted.
The live browser preview is the visual feedback surface; do not tell learners to open a terminal or run Judge0.
Keep Course 1 HTML-only. CSS and JavaScript may be mentioned as later layers but are never required for a correct answer.
Teach accessibility as part of normal markup: lang, headings, alt text, labels, link text, and semantic landmarks.
The capstone remains a single index.html page; multi-page navigation belongs in Practical HTML.

assessmentAndDelivery.suggestedBeginnerRhythm: One module per week or two short topics per study session.
assessmentAndDelivery.closingNote: Learners finish able to build a semantic, accessible HTML page and are ready for CSS.

modules.title: Final Capstone: Personal Website
modules.purpose: Bring the full HTML Foundations skill set together in one growing, cumulative, semantic, accessible multi-page website.
learningObjectives: Build one cumulative website whose files are introduced only when the project needs them.
Connect pages with meaningful navigation, relative links, and correctly referenced image assets.
Combine semantic structure, exact content, links, images, lists, tables, and a form appropriately.
Review document metadata, nesting, headings, labels, alt text, link text, and relative paths before submission.
Use the live browser preview and source validation to verify the complete final website.
guidedExercises: Start with index.html only and add new files only at the milestone where they become necessary
Carry every introduced file forward through the remaining milestones
Follow the exact learner-facing text, labels, links, table values, and form wording provided in each task
Use browser preview and cumulative source checks after each milestone

projectBrief.scenario: A local career-readiness mentor wants a polished personal portfolio website that can be reviewed before the learner moves on to CSS.
projectBrief.role: Beginner web developer responsible for building one portfolio website from a single Home page into a complete multi-page site.
projectBrief.workspace: A growing cumulative browser-web workspace. Start with index.html only. Add about.html in milestone 2; add projects/portfolio.html and images/profile.png in milestone 3; add contact.html in milestone 5. Once a file is introduced, keep it for every later milestone.
projectBrief.deliverable: One complete semantic and accessible multi-page personal portfolio website with meaningful navigation, correct relative paths, a real image asset, structured content, and a labeled contact form.
requirements: Use HTML only; do not require CSS or JavaScript for correctness.
Do not expose files before the milestone that needs them.
Once a file is introduced, keep it in every later starter and solution workspace.
Give learners the exact visible text, labels, navigation text, table values, and form wording required by each milestone.
Use index.html as the entry page for the entire project.
Use projects/portfolio.html as a nested page so the project practices ../ relative paths.
Use images/profile.png only from the milestone where the image becomes part of the website.
Use semantic landmarks, logical headings, meaningful links, useful alt text, structured content, and explicitly associated form labels.
Use live browser preview and source checks; do not require Judge0 or terminal execution.
